h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, מַאֲמָר ד׳ Rosh Chodesh Adar — Maamar Daled

p: בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ק׳ בִּשְׂחוֹק
In Sefer Yetzirah: “He crowned the letter Kuf with laughter,
etc., and Adar in the year.”
It says “laughter” and not a term of joy,
to fill his mouth with laughter in this world.”
And we must understand why laughter was created,
since it is forbidden in this world.
We have already said that it implies
that even for the sake of a mitzvah
it is forbidden to fill one’s mouth with laughter,
as they inferred there from the Baraisa:
it says “the joy of a mitzvah,”
and they did not say “the laughter of a mitzvah,”
though that is the subject under discussion;
this implies that laughter, even of a mitzvah, is forbidden.
about Rav Bruna, who rejoiced in mitzvos:
once he joined Geulah to Tefillah,
וְלָא פְּסִיק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא
and laughter did not leave his mouth all day.
How then was laughter permitted to him,
לְפִי הָאָמוּר דְּאַף שְׂחוֹק דְּמִצְוָה אָסוּר
according to what was said, that even laughter of a mitzvah is forbidden?
that laughter and joy are one matter,
only that joy is in the heart,
and laughter is the revealing of the joy in the heart.
And there is support for this from the Gemara
“From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed
there is no laughter for the Holy One, blessed be He.
And from where do we know there is no laughter?
Shall we say from what is written, etc.?
Perhaps it is forgetting that there is not,
but laughter, at least, there is.”
And the reading of the Ein Yaakov is
and it appears that his reading is the precise one,
for joy is the opposite of weeping and lament.
And what proof is there from joy to laughter?
only that joy is in the heart
and laughter is joy in revelation.
for the sake of a mitzvah is good,
“Let the heart of those who seek Hashem rejoice,”
“And their children shall see and rejoice,
their heart shall exult in Hashem.”
But laughter, the revealing of joy —
that will be only in the future,
“Then our mouth will be filled with laughter
וְרִנָּה הוּא גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה
and song too is a revealing of joy.
even in this world, songs and praises,
and Yisrael are praised for this:
they begin with words of Torah
וַהֲלֹא גַּם הָרִנָּה כְּתִיב אָז וְגוֹמֵר
Yet regarding song too it is written, “Then, etc.,
and from this verse he derives
דְּאָסוּר לְמַלֵּא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
that it is forbidden to fill one’s mouth with laughter in this world;
if so, the same applies to song,
that it ought to be forbidden in this world,
and according to the above, even song of a mitzvah.
However, in truth, the essential revealing of joy
will be only in the future,
meaning that there will shine and be revealed,
like the light of day, the attribute of Hu,
that is, Atika, the Concealed One,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רצ, א)
And in this world this aspect
and it will be revealed only in the future.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב נד, א)
the light of the Holy Ancient One
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ
And this is what it says: “Then our mouth will be filled with laughter
and our tongue with song” — “then,” Az, specifically.
So too on Shabbos, when there is a revelation of Atika,
as they said in the holy Zohar
(סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי חֵלֶק ג עט, ב
that the head of Zeir Anpin is filled
with the dew that descends from the Holy Ancient One
and drips into the Field of Holy Apples —
then the mouth too is opened
And this too is included in
what it says, “Then will be filled, etc.,”
for when there is a revelation of Atika
it is called Az, as mentioned above.
“But lips of knowledge are a precious vessel,”
“And by knowledge the chambers are filled
with all precious and pleasant wealth.”
is the inner dimension of Keser, as is known.
And we have already said many times
that through joining the wisdom in the mind
to the understanding in the heart,
one merits the aspect of Da’as,
and knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul.”
And this is the aspect of the revelation of Atika,
“‘And honor’ — these are the tefillin of the head,”
the head on which the tefillin rest
And this is what it says (Malachi 2:7):
“For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge,
and they seek Torah from his mouth.”
That is, the aspect of Da’as
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י (פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא לא, ג)
beyond the bounds of the wisdom in one’s mind.
a spirit from that Holy One Above,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג סא, א)
as they said in the holy Zohar (III 61a).
And then “they seek Torah from his mouth”:
“A sage is greater than a prophet.”
it is as though the Beis HaMikdash was built in his days.”
That is, whoever merits the aspect of Da’as,
since the yetzer hara has been cleared from his heart,
as they said in Tikkunei Zohar
in which the yetzer hara has its dwelling”;
and “My holy mountain” denotes the Beis HaMikdash.
וְהוּא כְּאִילּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו
So it is as though the Beis HaMikdash was built in his days —
And then the mouth is opened
to say songs and to sing,
And so it is called Az,
as it will be in the future.
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
אֶלָּא דַּעַת גָּנִיז בְּפוּמָא דְּמַלְכָּא וְכוּלֵּי
Rather, Da’as is hidden in the mouth of the King, etc.;
‘And by knowledge the chambers are filled,’ etc.
And when the light within it is awakened
וְנָפִיק כְּדֵין אִקְרֵי פֶּה ה׳ וְכוּלֵּי עַיֵּין שָׁם
and goes forth, then it is called ‘the mouth of Hashem,’ etc.” See there.
And this is what it says (Tehillim 51:17):
and my mouth will declare Your praise” —
according to the above, that to open the mouth
one must merit the aspect of Da’as,
for then it is called “the mouth of Hashem,”
(Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, maamar Pasach Eliyahu),
וְזֶה ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וּפִי וְגוֹמֵר
and this is “My Lord, open my lips, and my mouth, etc.”
And this too is the meaning of
for the joining does not mean in speech alone,
So what is so special about Rav Bruna,
that laughter did not leave his mouth?”
Rather, the matter is according to
what they said in the Yerushalmi
(בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ו יא, ב)
that one must mention in “Emes VeYatziv”
the splitting of the Yam Suf and the plague of the firstborn;
that is, regarding the Exodus from Egypt,
which we were commanded to remember constantly, every day;
the main point is the revelation of the light of Atika
that occurred in the plague of the firstborn,
We have already said many times
corresponding to the ten Sefiros, from below to above,
[רְאֵה זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב לו, א]
and in the plague of the firstborn
Yisrael went out from the beginning of the kelipah
namely the light of Keser Elyon.
And so too with the splitting of the Yam Suf,
that the splitting of the Yam Suf depends on Atika;
and it is stated in the Mechilta (Parshas HaShirah 3)
that is, to gaze upon the Merkavah,
which is hidden from all thought.
And this must be joined to Tefillah,
in which one stands before the King,
and Tefillah is of the attribute of Malchus,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וְגוֹמֵר
as it says, “My Lord, open my lips, etc.”
And then, when he merits the aspect of Da’as,
the light within it is awakened,
and then it is called “the mouth of Hashem,”
as we cited from the holy Zohar;
and then the Shechinah will speak
the words of prayer from within his throat,
as we have said many times
in the name of our master, Rabbi Elimelech,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing,
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל
that this is the meaning of “the Holy One, blessed be He, prays” —
[בְּרָכוֹת ז, א] הַיְינוּ בְּתוֹךְ פִּיפִיּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
(Berachos 7a) — namely, within the mouths of Yisrael.
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Berachos 4b):
זֶה הַסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאוּלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית לִתְפִלָּה וְכוּלֵּי
One who joins the Geulah of Maariv to Tefillah, etc.”
Now Tosafos already raised a difficulty
“destined for the life of the World to Come” —
have a share in the World to Come
לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עַל לְשׁוֹן בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא
that this does not apply to the expression “ben Olam Haba.”
“ben Olam Haba” is to be explained
that he will be, in the present, right away,
who attains of the light of the future,
שֶׁיָּאִיר לוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּחִינַת הוּא
that the aspect of Hu shine for him in this world,
that is, that he merit the aspect of Da’as.
וְהוּא כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א)
It is akin to what they said (Berachos 17a):
“May you see your world in your lifetime,”
which we explained means that they blessed him
that he merit, in this world,
a semblance of the revelation of the World to Come.
And one merits this when he joins Geulah to Tefillah,
which is the splitting of the Yam Suf
and the plague of the firstborn,
which come from the light of Atika;
and he merits the revelation of the light of Da’as,
to be “My Lord, open my lips,” as said
to be as in the World to Come,
joy in revealed form is permitted to him.
And this is what they said about Rav Bruna,
that he joined Geulah to Tefillah:
meaning that he merited the aspect of Da’as
and the revelation of the light of Atika,
וְהוּא כְּאִלּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו
and it was as though the Beis HaMikdash was built in his days,
וּכְבָר הוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא בַּהוֹו
and he was already a ben Olam Haba in the present.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּתַּר לוֹ הַשִּׂמְחָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
Therefore revealed joy was permitted to him,
and this is what they said: laughter did not leave
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בַּמִּדְבָּר חֵלֶק ג קיח, א)
And in the holy Zohar (Bamidbar, III 118a):
except at the time when Yisrael
dwell in the Holy Land, etc.”
the point is that he merited the aspect of Da’as,
and it is as though the Beis HaMikdash was built in his days —
all the more so is it like
the time when Yisrael dwell in Eretz Yisrael,
as they said in the holy Zohar (ibid.).
And then joy too is permitted
in revealed form, with song and laughter.
And this is what they said:
“He crowned the letter Kuf with laughter.”
For it is stated in the holy Zohar
“A hundred years — the sum of all,
the Holy One, blessed be He, who is comprised
from the supernal place, most hidden of all hidden,
in a hundred, in the secret
of the hundred blessings of each day.”
And we said that this refers to Atika,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ [חֵלֶק ב פט, א]
which is called in the holy Zohar (II 89a)
That is, the number one hundred
is the number of ultimate completeness:
עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת כְּשֶׁכָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר
the ten Sefiros, when each one is comprised of ten.
And so it is stated in the holy Zohar
that she makes from them a crown
and places it on the head
of the Tzaddik, Life of the Worlds,
“Blessings upon the head of the tzaddik”;
and this too refers to the attribute of Atika —
“the head of the tzaddik” alludes to Atika.
וְאָז הַזְּמַן יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ כָּאָמוּר
And then is the time when “our mouth will be filled with laughter,” as said;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ק׳ בִּשְׂחוֹק
and this is what they said: “He crowned the letter Kuf with laughter.”
And in the Osiyos of Rabbi Akiva, on the letter Kuf,
the father of the sages, etc.,
He expounds Kuf as from hikif, “encompassed.”
of blessed memory (in his glosses on the holy Zohar),
on what they said in the holy Zohar
the secret of the Great Serpent,
which is the Arich of the kelipah.
And then Yisrael were in Egypt
like a fetus in its mother’s womb,
as they said in the Pesikta (Parashah 15)
“a nation from the midst of a nation”;
that is, the kelipah surrounded Yisrael.
the wisdom of Egypt then held sway,
and the wisdom of the Torah was there
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who encompassed Pharaoh with his wisdom,
the wisdom of the Torah from there, from their midst.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
is in the secret of Da’as, as is known;
and this is what they said, “He crowned
the letter Kuf with laughter,” as said.
And so in the month of Adar is the obliteration of Amalek,
for the kelipah of Amalek is “first of the nations,”
the beginning of the kelipah, like Pharaoh;
only Pharaoh is the Arich of the kelipah of desire,
and Amalek the Arich of the kelipah of jealousy,
anger and murder (and this was explained in Yisro, maamar 3).
And Amalek’s way is that he can conceal himself
so thoroughly that he misleads a person
and he disguises himself as one guiding him to good,
in the manner of what they said (Chullin 91a):
“He appeared to him as a talmid chacham” —
for he disguised himself as a rabbi showing the way
(and this was explained in Bo, maamar 1).
which is hidden from all thought,
and then they will be able to conquer
as they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 104a),
Yisrael merit the revelation of Atika,
the most hidden of all hidden,
in the secret of one hundred, as said;
and then it is the time for obliterating Amalek,
like a monkey beside human beings
and the heart becomes “My holy mountain,”
and then “our mouth will be filled with laughter,”

paragraphs.text: Ein Yaakov, Avodah Zarah 3b — “Rav Acha of Galilee said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: According to the view that, since the Temple was destroyed, there is no laughter before the Holy One, blessed be He, what does He do in the fourth quarter? He sits and teaches Torah to schoolchildren. From where do we know that there is no laughter before Him? ... Perhaps it is forgetting that does not occur, but joy still occurs! Rather, from here: 'I have kept silent from of old; I shall be still and restrain Myself.'” This retrieved Ein Yaakov text reads 'joy' at the critical question, where the standard Avodah Zarah 3b text reads 'laughter.' The actual variant is therefore verified. Rav Tzadok uses it as evidence that joy and laughter name the same inner content at different degrees of disclosure.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 12b — “'On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine'—was his heart not merry with wine until now? Rava said: The seventh day was Shabbos. When Israel eat and drink, they begin with words of Torah and praise; when the nations eat and drink, they begin with frivolous matters.” Rav Tzadok raises a concrete difficulty from the Gemara's praise of Shabbos song: if outward joy is reserved for the future, how is present song possible? His answer turns on Shabbos as a disclosure of the future light.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Idra Zuta, III 290a — “Because in Atika there is neither beginning nor end, it is not called 'You'; because it is concealed and not revealed, it is called 'He.' From the place where a beginning is found it is called 'You' and is called Father, as it is written: 'For You are our Father.' In the teaching of the school of Rav Yeiva the Elder: In the inclusive account, Zeir Anpin is called 'You,' while the concealed Holy Ancient One is called 'He.'” The distinction of 'You' from the concealed 'He' is explicit in the retrieved original. Rav Tzadok interprets the future 'that day' as the day on which this concealed level will be illumined. The traditional III 290a locator follows the manuscript; this particular Idra extract has no embedded page overlay.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 16b — “'And honor'—these are tefillin, as it is said: 'All the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you, and they shall fear you.' Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin of the head.” The maamar now develops the 'honor' clause, beyond its earlier treatment of light and joy. The head-tefillin image permits Rav Tzadok's association with the supernal crown.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 43 — “‘To know (le'de'ah) what would be done to him’—it should have said ‘to see’; so it was through ruach hakodesh … this is da'as, the inner aspect of Keser.” Citing the Mechilta (‘de'ah is nothing but ruach hakodesh’), Rav Tzadok gives the Midrashic basis for equating da'as with ruach hakodesh, which is assumed here. Miriam's ‘standing’ by the river was da'as from above, beyond what the mind could see.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 61a, Acharei Mos — “What is Holy? The perfection of everything, called supernal Wisdom. From that place holy anointing flows through known paths to the place called supernal Understanding. From there springs and streams issue on every side until they reach this zot.... When this zot is blessed ... it is called the Holy Spirit: that is, a spirit from that higher Holy. When mysteries of Torah issue and awaken from it, it is called the Holy Tongue.” The source itself explains the compound expression ruach hakodesh as a spirit flowing from supernal holiness, and immediately relates it to the emergence of Torah mysteries.

paragraphs.text: Ramban, Chiddushim, Bava Basra 12a — “This is what it means: Although the prophecy of the prophets, which is the appearance and vision, was taken away, the prophecy of the sages, which comes through the path of wisdom, was not taken away. Rather, they know the truth through the Divine inspiration within them. For on occasion He rests His Divine Presence even upon the pious who are not sages.” Ramban distinguishes visionary prophecy from the sages' apprehension of truth through wisdom and inner Divine inspiration. The Gemara immediately adds, 'A sage is greater than a prophet.' Rav Tzadok draws on this distinction for the inspired quality of Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 14b — “Esther—for it is written, 'On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty.' Should it not have said 'royal garments'? Rather, Divine inspiration clothed her. Here it is written 'clothed,' and there it is written 'A spirit clothed Amasai.'” The source makes malchus, royalty, a manifestation of ruach hakodesh in Esther's action. It thus gives Rav Tzadok a direct Purim example for the link among Malchus, inspired apprehension, and its expression.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a — “These are two Shabbosos, corresponding to the upper and lower Divine Presence. 'To make Shabbos for their generations'—what is 'for their generations'? Happy is the person who makes them a dwelling on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, and from there the evil inclination, which is the profanation of Shabbos, is cleared away. paragraphs.text: Zohar II 123a, Mishpatim — “What is the mouth? Knowledge is hidden in the King's mouth, which is called Tiferes, the extension of Tiferes in which all treasures and all colors are united, as it is written: 'Through knowledge the chambers are filled.' That knowledge is hidden in the King's mouth and fills all chambers and porticoes. When its illumination awakens and comes forth, it is called 'the mouth of Hashem.' The lips, the two lights from Father and Mother, when they meet in that illumination of knowledge, join together, and words are decreed in truth, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge.” The source explicitly links concealed knowledge with its emergence as true speech. Rav Tzadok uses that movement in explaining 'My Lord, open my lips.'

paragraphs.text: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3, on Exodus 15:2 — “Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see? ... It is like a mortal king entering a province, surrounded by his guard, mighty men to his right and left, and armies before and behind him. Everyone asks, 'Which one is the king?' because he is flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed at the sea, none needed to ask, 'Which is He?' As soon as they saw Him, they recognized Him, and all opened their mouths and said: 'This is my God, and I shall glorify Him.'” The distinctive point is immediate recognition that issues in song. The corresponding Zohar passage, Beshalach 31:434, within the II 64b overlay, repeats that a maidservant saw what Yechezkel did not see; its exact original has also been retrieved.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — “May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be life in the World to Come, your hope for every generation. May your eyes shine with the light of Torah and your face radiate like the brightness of the firmament; may your lips express knowledge, your innermost parts rejoice in uprightness, and your steps run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days.” This blessing distinguishes seeing one's world during life from one's final life in the World to Come. Its conjunction of understanding, speech, song, and the Ancient of Days particularly illuminates Rav Tzadok's present interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Otiyos DeRabbi Akiva, version I, letter kuf — “Kuf—this is Moshe, father of the sages, father of all the prophets. Father of all the sages, who set before Pharaoh every matter of wisdom, understanding, counsel, knowledge, and discernment in seventy languages. Seventy scribes wrote in seventy languages, and every document stood before Pharaoh the wicked. When they saw Moshe and Aharon, resembling ministering angels, ... with the staff of God in their hand and the explicit Name engraved upon it, ... fear and trembling immediately fell upon them.” The original alphabet Midrash is preserved in Otzar Midrashim, New York 1915. Rav Tzadok attends to the play between kuf and hikif, surrounding or encompassing, and reads Moshe's wisdom as encompassing Pharaoh's.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 107:4 — “Rabbi Abahu son of Rabbi Acha said in the name of our master: Thus Israel were placed within Egypt like a fetus placed within the innards of an animal. Just as the shepherd puts his hand into its innards and draws it out, so did the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, ‘to take for Himself a nation from the midst of a nation.’” The same simile appears in Midrash Tehillim 114:3, in Rabbi Abba bar Acha's name in Rabbi Chanin's name: “Like a person who draws the fetus out from an animal's womb.” Rav Tzadok himself cites this simile elsewhere from Shocher Tov 107 (Resisei Layla; Divrei Soferim). Pesikta Rabbasi 15 (HaChodesh), like Pesikta deRav Kahana 5:11, expounds the same verse: “these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised; these grew forelocks and those grew forelocks.” It does not contain the fetal comparison. The Pesikta reference therefore supports the exposition of “a nation from the midst of a nation,” and the simile itself comes from Midrash Tehillim.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Purim, “Shushan Purim,” s.v. Inyan perazim umukkafim (digital 4:2–4) — “My revered father and teacher explained that there are two kinds of evil inclination. One incites a person toward what is forbidden: even though he knows that he has been warned against it, it incites him to transgress Hashem's command. This is ‘he appeared to him as a gentile.’ Another evil inclination presents reasons that this is permitted, and perhaps even a mitzvah. This is ‘he appeared to him as a Torah scholar.’ Thus far his words. … It is written, ‘A breached city without a wall is a person who has no restraint over his spirit.’ A walled place therefore alludes to a person who has restraint over his spirit. This counters the first husk. But against the second husk, which presents reasons that the impure is pure, the wall has no advantage.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Shem MiShmuel applies the same disguise as a Torah scholar to Purim and Amalek, distinguishing weakness of restraint from a corrupted judgment that represents sin as a mitzvah. His wall image shows why stronger restraint alone cannot answer the latter: a person may be disciplined while obeying a false religious guide. This clarifies the particular need Rav Tzadok identifies for a deeper disclosure that unmasks a concealed root of evil. The parallel illustrates that need without equating Shem MiShmuel's explanation with Rav Tzadok's specific account of Atika.
